title: Recovered CYMBA / neurostimulation earbud design requirements
status: Accepted design direction followed by an explicitly provisional engineering blueprint. No later message freezing numerical specifications was found in the retrieved turns.
acceptedDirection: Compact, conventional-looking premium wired IEM with high-quality music playback, including when stimulation is off.
Modular acoustic and neural interfaces: independently replaceable EEG-capable acoustic tip and soft concha/cymba stimulation wing.
Replaceable shallow silicone tip with electrically separate dry recording contact areas against the outer canal; appropriate reference/bias contacts still require design.
Soft concha/cymba wing carrying two electrically isolated stimulation contacts.
One inward-facing reflective PPG sensor initially, in one ear; location remains a candidate requiring validation.
External clip-on or desk controller with physical controls; USB-C DAC, stimulation control, processing and sensing interface.
Keep audio path, stimulation contacts, EEG interfaces and PPG optical path distinct.

provisionalTargets.driver: One professionally tuned 7–10 mm dynamic driver
provisionalTargets.eeg: Initially one useful differential channel, with appropriate reference/bias
provisionalTargets.ppg: One reflective optical sensor in one ear
provisionalTargets.anc: Later, if acoustic and EEG integration permit
provisionalTargets.personalisation: Task-aware research controller; EEG assistance only if validated

currentUserOverrides: Cable exits BOTTOM of each earbud and hangs down; no over-ear cable routing.
Use the compact smooth-faced industrial design in design-reference.png.
prototypeSequence: Preserve an existing premium IEM's acoustic assembly and stock audio cable.
Add a reversible cradle and passive soft wing; assess fit and audio.
Validate stimulation and sensing using appropriate separate research systems.
Only then develop custom integrated housing and electronics.
visualisationLimits: Internal packaging, contact geometry, exact electrode count/reference placement and electronics layouts remain illustrative.
Do not infer automatic or proven cognitive improvement from sensing or stimulation.
Do not depict the draft render as CAD or a construction schematic.
